items.title: AI isn’t Asia’s only game in town
items.author: Manishi Raychaudhuri
items.creator: Manishi Raychaudhuri
items.summary: As doubts mount over Asia's AI boom, some of the region's strongest returns are building far from the hype. While tech dominates the headlines, old-economy mainstays are also key drivers of the broader market story.
items.body:
As doubts mount over [USN:L1N4230I4 TEXT:"Asia's AI boom"], some of the region's strongest returns are building far from the hype. While tech dominates the headlines, old-economy mainstays are also key drivers of the broader market story.
Technology accounts for six of Asia's 15 best-performing market sectors in 2026 thus far. But the remaining nine tell a non-tech story anchored in financials, energy, industrials and process industries.
Admittedly, some of these themes overlap with the AI capital expenditure juggernaut. For example, investments in power generation, grid infrastructure and industrial cooling are clearly being propelled by data centre needs.
But AI is not the only driver of these old-economy investment sweet spots, as geopolitical unrest and high energy prices are also playing a role. Fears about a slowdown in the tech boom may rattle Asian markets — as we saw [USN:L1N45Z05C TEXT:"last week"] — but they will not necessarily bring the Asian surge to a screeching halt.
DEFENCE AND INFRASTRUCTURE Rising global defence spending has been a major investment driver worldwide this year, as military tensions escalate, most notably in the Middle East and Europe.
This trend has been building ever since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and has skyrocketed as US President Donald Trump has put more pressure on European allies to increase defence spending.
North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) members, which account for 65% of global defence expenditure, committed in June 2025 to raise their annual defence spending to 5% of gross domestic product by 2035. Global defence spending represented only 2.4% of global GDP in 2025.
The widening conflict in the Middle East, which escalated following the US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, has also highlighted the vulnerability of countries throughout the Gulf.
Asian defence manufacturers stand to gain from this global defence spending boom as Western capacity constraints potentially give Asian rivals an edge in delivery times and prices for comparable equipment.
According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, South Korea supplied 8.6% of all arms imported by European NATO members during 2021–25, ahead of Israel's 7.7% and France's 7.4%. This came as Europe's overall arms imports roughly tripled.
At the same time, “insourcing” of defence manufacturing – creating a homegrown military-industrial complex – is already a trend in several Asian nations. India aims for 70% defence "indigenisation" by 2027, Indonesia seeks 60% local content in defence equipment by 2030, and Vietnam is targeting 50% domestic inputs in select armaments by 2030.
Increasing defence needs and military modernization are also spurring a broader infrastructure buildout globally. This includes reinforced bridges, roads, ports and railways, which are needed to transport heavy equipment, alongside fortified energy grids, telecommunications services, and cyber networks.
McKinsey forecasts $106 trillion in global infrastructure investment through 2040, with Asia accounting for roughly 65% of that. The region's domestic industry has several advantages, including local ties, inexpensive state financing and integrated operations that can lower costs and speed delivery.
Asia’s own infrastructure buildout could be mammoth too. Regional transport infrastructure alone could require investment of $2.6 trillion annually through 2035, according to the Asian Transport Observatory and the Asian Development Bank. That would represent more than three times the roughly $800 billion annual average spent from 2020 to 2025.
Reflecting these trends, the order books of major Asian industrial and defence groups — including Larsen & Toubro , Hanwha Aerospace (012450.KS) and China Railway Group — already stand at several times annual revenue, supporting a robust growth outlook.
GREEN GLOBALIZATION The global drive for energy independence should also benefit Asia, the leader in clean energy technologies. The stickiness of crude oil prices above $100 a barrel – and the related shock of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz this year – should push more consumers, businesses and governments toward renewables, particularly solar power, battery energy storage, offshore wind and electric vehicles.
While Chinese companies currently dominate this space, fierce domestic competition, termed "involution," has dampened their margins, just as trade friction with the US and Europe has led to higher tariffs.
Companies best positioned may be those with significant overseas revenue and well-established foreign manufacturing facilities and supply chains that can overcome tariff walls and trade restrictions. According to FactSet, Chinese EV makers BYD and Geely (0175.HK) draw 43% and 23% of their respective revenue from abroad, while Chinese battery titan CATL (300750.SZ) generates 34% of its revenue overseas.
CAVEAT EMPTOR This strategy is no slam dunk, of course. Swapping AI exposure for heavy industry and state-backed defence does not eliminate risk — it merely trades tech valuation hype for other more familiar hazards.
Defence and infrastructure orders come mostly from governments, raising the risk of bureaucratic delays, cost overruns, and abrupt legislative budget cuts. On the green energy front, the risk remains that Asia’s fierce domestic price wars could spread outward when companies compete in foreign markets.
Meanwhile, prolonged inflation, elevated energy prices and high interest rates could slow infrastructure buildouts and trigger corporate defaults. And a truly massive AI pullback could have ripple effects across the region’s markets.
Yet, for now, Asia's old economy continues to offer genuine substance beyond all the tech-driven hype.
(The views expressed here are those of Manishi Raychaudhuri , the founder and CEO of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd and the former head of Asia-Pacific Equity Research at BNP Paribas Securities.)

items.title: 米アンソロピック、ＡＩの安全性確保に向けた法案を議員に提案＝報道
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１６日 ロイター] - 米ニュースサイトのポリティコは１６日、人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックの代表者が、最先端...
items.body:
米アンソロピック、ＡＩの安全性確保に向けた法案を議員に提案＝報道
7:59 配信

写真は米アンソロピックのイベントブース。9月17日、米カリフォルニア州サンフランシスコで撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

[１６日 ロイター] - 米ニュースサイトのポリティコは１６日、人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックの代表者が、最先端ＡＩモデルの安全性とセキュリティーを確保する法案の導入に向け、米議会議員らに草案を働きかけていると報じた。事情に詳しい３人の情報筋の話だとしている。

この法案には、ＡＩモデルが１０億ドルを超える損害をもたらすか、５０人以上の死亡または重傷を負わせることにつながる予見可能かつ差し迫ったリスクをもたらす場合に限り、政府が公開や使用を阻止できるようにすることを定めた。

詳細は下記の通り。

・ポリティコによると、提案された草案は生物兵器の製造や導入を防いだり、ＡＩモデルが制御やサイバー攻撃を回避したりすることを目的としている。

・アンソロピックの広報担当者はロイターに対し、アンソロピックが今年発表した「先進ＡＩフレームワーク」に盛り込んだ提案を草案に反映していると説明した。

・この広報担当者によると、草案は政府に対して「最も強力なＡＩモデルの危険な展開を阻止または抑止する能力」を与えるとともに、開発者に対して最先端ＡＩモデルの訓練の実施や、結果の透明性確保、および第三者による評価を得ることを義務付ける。

・商務省は、ロイターからのコメント要請に直ちには回答しなかった。

・報道によると、商務省に登録された独立した評価機関が、最先端ＡＩモデルと開発機関を定期的に評価する役割を担うと草案に盛り込まれた。

・良い評価結果を得るための買収行為がない限り、開発機関がこれらの評価機関に報酬を支払うことができることも記載されている。

・評価機関が最先端ＡＩモデルに「差し迫った具体的なリスク」があると判断した場合、評価完了から７２時間以内に商務省に報告しなければならないと明記している。

・商務省は危険性があることを認定した場合、裁判官に対してＡＩモデルの停止を要請することができる。草案には、他のいかなる米政府、機関、または職員も開発、導入、または内部利用を停止することを禁じると定めた。

・首都ワシントンの連邦地裁の裁判官がＡＩモデルの停止を命じることができる権限を持つと草案に定めた。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１８日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトが英クラウドサービス企業エヌスケールとのデータセンター契約から撤退したと、英...
items.body:
米マイクロソフト、英データセンター契約から撤退＝英紙
7:48 配信

マイクロソフトのロゴ。2025年3月、パリ近郊イッシーレムリノーの同社オフィスで撮影。REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

[１８日 ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトが英クラウドサービス企業エヌスケールとのデータセンター契約から撤退したと、英紙テレグラフが１８日に報じた。

同紙によると、マイクロソフトはエヌスケールの２大顧客の１社で、英エセックス州ラウトンのデータセンターに関する契約を最近解除した。

同紙は撤退の理由に言及していない。マイクロソフトはロイターに対し、コメントを控えた。

テレグラフによると、エヌスケールは同プロジェクトで度重なる遅延に直面していた。英送電網担当者は同社に対し、データセンターへの電力供給が２０３０年代まで見込めないと伝えていたという。

エヌスケールの広報担当者はロイターに対し、「マイクロソフトとの関係は引き続き強固で長期的なものだ。今回のロンドン全域の送電網問題は残念だが、他の契約には影響しない」と述べた。

「ラウトンの事業と英国への取り組みを引き続き堅持している。英国での他の拡張候補地に加え、同施設向けの代替電源も検討している」と説明した。

エヌスケールは９月、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を申請した。目論見書によると、マイクロソフトとアンソロピックが主要顧客となる見通し。

エヌスケールは、計算資源や電力、データセンターなどのインフラに加え、人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルの学習や稼働に使うソフトウエアを提供している。

エヌビディアが出資する同社は、コアウィーブ、ネビウス、クルーソー、ラムダと競合する。設立以降急成長しており、わずか２年半で契約総額は１億ドルから１０３０億ドル超に拡大した。

items.title: NFL roundup: Browns edge Ravens to grab share of AFC North lead
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
items.body:
Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
Deshaun Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy on a 33-yard pass to the Baltimore 29-yard line with 22 seconds remaining to set up the decisive kick.
Szmyt's initial attempt from 42 yards was blocked by Keyon Martin, who was flagged for offside. Szmyt then drilled his second attempt through the uprights.
Carson Schwesinger racked up 13 tackles and forced a fumble for the Browns (4-2), who are tied with the Ravens (4-2) and Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) atop the division.
Watson was 16-for-26 for 164 yards as Cleveland halted a three-game slide against Baltimore. Tyler "Snoop" Huntley completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown for the Ravens as he started in place of Lamar Jackson (ankle) for the second straight week.
Steelers 26, Buccaneers 19 (OT)
Aaron Rodgers threw touchdown passes in the fourth quarter and overtime and Chris Boswell made four field goals to lead Pittsburgh to a comeback win in overtime over host Tampa Bay.
The Steelers erased a 16-3 fourth quarter deficit with 16 straight points in the period. The Bucs tied the game at 19 with three seconds left on a 53-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin. In overtime, Rodgers led a 12-play, 70-yard drive, capped by a 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard with 3:15 left in overtime. Bernard caught 11 passes for 87 yards and DK Metcalf caught 11 passes for 93 yards.
Jalon Daniels, who made his third consecutive start for injured Baker Mayfield (thumb), was sacked on fourth down by Jalen Ramsey on a corner blitz to end the game. Pittsburgh's defense sacked Daniels five times and intercepted him twice. Daniels completed 22 of 43 for 164 and a touchdown.
Bears 31, Falcons 23
Caleb Williams returned from a three-game absence to complete 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown to help visiting Chicago stave off Atlanta.
Williams showed little rust after suffering a hamstring tear on Sept. 20, connecting with eight different receivers for the Bears, who won their third game in four tries. D'Andre Swift rushed for two touchdowns for Chicago, which saw its 24-point fourth-quarter lead dwindle to eight before holding on.
Michael Penix Jr. completed 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns for Atlanta, which dropped its second straight. He threw two touchdown passes to Kyle Pitts Sr. and a pair of two-point conversion passes to slice the Bears' lead to eight with 5:41 to play.
Texans 34, Jaguars 31
CJ Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns to set the stage for Ka'imi Fairbairn's game-winning 49-yard field goal as time expired, helping Houston pull out a narrow win over Jacksonville in London.
Stroud completed 24 of 34 passes with one interception. Tight end Foster Moreau caught two passes, both touchdowns, while Jaylin Noel had a career-high 107 receiving yards and a touchdown for the Texans.
Trevor Lawrence completed 24 of 41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one pick for the Jaguars, who had their three-game winning streak snapped. Bhayshul Tuten had 39 rushing yards and four catches for 48 yards and two TD catches. Travis Hunter Jr. became the first NFL player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 with a TD catch and interception in the same game.
Titans 26, Colts 20
Joey Slye connected on a tie-breaking 49-yard field goal with 2:03 left as visiting Tennessee upset Indianapolis for its first win of the season.
Slye added a 44-yarder with 43 seconds remaining for his fourth field goal after Tennessee got a fourth-down stop. The comeback from a 13-point halftime deficit gave head coach Robert Saleh his first win with the club. Amani Hooker finished with a career-high 13 tackles and an interception while Tennessee notched six sacks.
Daniel Jones hit 22 of 42 passes for 269 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for Indianapolis while Jonathan Taylor ran for 94 yards on 21 carries. That included a game-tying 4-yard touchdown with 5:32 to play.
Patriots 26, Jets 19
Drake Maye tossed three touchdown passes and New England extended its winning streak to three games with a home victory over New York.
Maye completed 18 of 32 passes for 235 yards. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry had New England's touchdown receptions, while Douglas caught seven passes for 86 yards.
New York's Geno Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown but was intercepted for the first time this season. The Jets received four field goals from Jason Sanders and a game-high 11 tackles (six solo) from Jamien Sherwood.
Panthers 25, Eagles 14
Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and Carolina's defense was solid in a road victory over short-handed Philadelphia.
Young finished 20-for-39 for 281 yards. Backfield mate Chuba Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries and Ryan Fitzgerald kicked two long field goals to help the Panthers to their second road triumph in three tries this season.
Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in his season debut for the Eagles, who lost their fourth consecutive game. McKee filled in for Jalen Hurts (blood clot), who was placed on injured reserve Saturday. The Eagles punted eight times and collected 17 first downs.
Saints 34, Giants 27
Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a TD and visiting New Orleans held off the New York Giants.
The Saints ended a three-game losing streak as they rushed for a season-high 175 yards and Martin Emerson Jr. had two of the team's three interceptions. Shough completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and connected with Bryce Lance, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave for scores after the Giants took a 10-0 lead.
Jameis Winston passed for one touchdown and two interceptions for the Giants before being replaced by J.J. McCarthy, who led a dramatic late comeback. McCarthy, who completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, piloted three scoring drives and a fourth drive which stalled at the Saints 14-yard line in the waning seconds. Malik Nabers finished with 12 catches for 165 yards for New York.
Cardinals 18, Rams 16
Arizona received a career-best six field goals from Chad Ryland, including the game winner from 43 yards as time expired, to earn a victory over Los Angeles in Inglewood, Calif.
Jacoby Brissett completed 24 of 35 passes for 218 yards with an interception, while leading the Cardinals on a game-winning 40-yard scoring drive in the closing minute. Bam Knight rushed for 80 yards on 15 carries for Arizona (2-4), which has seen both of its wins this season come in the Los Angeles area after a Week 1 road victory over the Chargers.
Matthew Stafford completed 25 of 33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns but struggled to get the Rams offense going against a blitzing Cardinals defense. Puka Nacua had six receptions for 80 yards for Los Angeles (2-4). The Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe, who replaced Harrison Mevis after he was cut earlier in the week, in the first quarter when he injured his knee on a kickoff and did not return.
Chiefs 22, Chargers 6
Kenneth Walker III rushed for 128 yards and two touchdowns and Patrick Mahomes passed for 272 yards to boost Kansas City past visiting Los Angeles.
The Chiefs (5-0) remain the lone unbeaten team in the AFC. Mahomes was 23-for-30 through the air while earning his 100th win as a starting quarterback. Kansas City sacked Chargers QB Justin Herbert four times, matching its season total entering the game.
Herbert was 22-for-37 for 204 yards and an interception. He also led Los Angeles with 26 yards on five carries. Cameron Dicker kicked field goals of 23 and 30 yards. The skidding Chargers (0-6) are off to the franchise's worst start since the 2000 San Diego Chargers lost their first 11 games during a 1-15 season. Current head coach Jim Harbaugh started five games at quarterback for that team.
Bills 33, Raiders 30
Josh Allen threw two touchdown passes, James Cook rushed for 95 yards and the go-ahead touchdown, and Buffalo beat host Las Vegas.
Allen completed 23 of 33 passes for 255 yards, and tight end Dalton Kincaid had seven receptions for 38 yards. Keon Coleman caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown for the Bills (5-1).
For the Raiders (3-3), Kirk Cousins completed 23 of 41 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns to Tre Tucker, who caught five passes for 97 yards. Tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer combined for 11 receptions and 165 yards. Las Vegas cut into the deficit on Tucker's diving 44-yard touchdown with 1:32 left before failing to recover the onside kick.
--Field Level Media
--Field Level Media

items.title: 再送-スバル、20年代後半にＳＤⅤ投入、開発期間も4割短縮
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
(重複した部分を削除して再送します)

Maki Shiraki

[佐野市（栃木県） １９日 ロイター] - ＳＵＢＡ...
items.body:
再送-スバル、20年代後半にＳＤⅤ投入、開発期間も4割短縮
7:42 配信

写真はＳＵＢＡＲＵ（スバル）のロゴ。4月1日、米ニューヨーク市で撮影。REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

(重複した部分を削除して再送します)

Maki Shiraki

[佐野市（栃木県） １９日 ロイター] - ＳＵＢＡＲＵ（スバル）は、２０２０年代後半にソフトウエア定義車両（ＳＤＶ）を投入する。ＳＤＶの中核となる新開発の制御統合ＥＣＵ（電子制御ユニット）を全車種に順次搭載する。ハードウエア、ソフトウエア、実車検証を一体で進める開発手法に切り替え、車両開発に要する期間を現状より約４割短縮する。１８日の開発戦略説明会で方針を示した。

同社は今後、制御統合ＥＣＵを通じて独自の運転支援機能「アイサイト」と「走る・曲がる・止まる」に直結する車両制御を高度化し、購入後も無線通信によるソフトウエアの更新（ＯＴＡ）を通じて車を進化させる。 制御統合ＥＣＵの核となる半導体は米アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイシス（ＡＭＤ）と共同開発した。ＡＩ（人工知能）の活用や高性能半導体の採用はコスト上昇要因となるが、半導体を含む技術の内製化を進め、 電気自動車（ＥＶ）、ハイブリッド車、ガソリン車で電子プラットフォームを全車共通化するなどして価格を抑える。

柴田英司常務執行役員は、ＯＴＡによって運転支援、自動運転、走行性能などの機能を高め、「使えば使うほど、どんどん車自体が良くなっていくことを狙う」と述べた。

ＳＤＶを巡っては、スバルに約２１％出資するトヨタ自動車が独自のソフトウェアプラットフォーム（基盤）「アリーン」を新車に搭載し、３０年までに世界で販売する全車種をＳＤＶにする計画を掲げており、３５年には提携先などの車にもアリーンを展開したい考えを示している。スバルは現時点でアリーンを採用する計画はない。

車両開発期間の４割短縮に向けては、車両の試作工程をデジタルシミュレーションに置き換える。設計、開発車両の実車検証、量産準備といった各工程を順番に進めるのではなく、同時並行的に進める。デジタルシミュレーションやＡＩを活用しつつ、実車で走行性能や安全性の検証時間も確保する。ＥＶやＳＤＶへの対応が急がれる中、限られた資源で商品投入のスピードと競争力を高める。

中国勢は約２年と従来より大幅に短い周期でＥＶの新型車を投入し、価格競争力や運転支援技術、コネクテッド機能を進化させている。スバルは、部品や車台の共通化、デジタル技術の活用を進め、品質を維持しながら開発の迅速化とコスト低減を図る。

乾保常務執行役員は、スバルとしては単純に開発期間の短さを競うのではなく、「仮に開発期間が若干長くても、しっかり市場の要望に応えていく柔軟性を持ちたい」と説明。「最終的な商品のこだわりにかける時間をアジャイル（柔軟）に、いかにその短期（の開発期間）の中に入れ込められるか」が勝負になるとの考えを示した。

開発現場では、部門や取引先との間で設計を順番に引き渡す従来の方法を改め、同じ場所・情報・目標を共有するチームで開発を進める体制に移行し、車種ごとに個別最適化してきた開発の在り方を見直す。車種間の部品共用率を５０％にして部品点数を減らし、デジタルを活用するなどして生産性を現状から倍増させる。

items.title: Anthropic planea destinar el 5% de sus acciones a un fondo de beneficio público
items.author: Katrina Manson
items.summary: La startup detrás de Claude creará un fondo de beneficio público que crecerá junto con su valoración y podrá financiar iniciativas para mitigar los efectos de la IA en el mercado laboral.
items.body: Bloomberg — Anthropic PBC anunció que planea destinar el 5% de sus acciones a un nuevo fondo de beneficio público que le permitirá realizar donaciones para el bien común, incluyendo la mitigación del impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral. El anuncio se produce mientras la startup de inteligencia artificial de rápido crecimiento se prepara para una salida a bolsa que se prevé sea una de las mayores de la historia. Al mismo tiempo, Anthropic busca abordar las crecientes preocupaciones sobre la seguridad de la IA y su posible impacto no deseado —desde ciberataques hasta la pérdida masiva de empleos— a medida que las empresas adoptan agentes de IA que pueden reemplazar la mano de obra humana. Ver más: Anthropic habría presentado proyecto de ley para frenar modelos de IA que amenacen vidas o causen daños El nuevo Fondo Antropológico de Beneficio Público podría permitir a la empresa llevar a cabo su misión “de nuevas maneras”, como por ejemplo, utilizando parte del dinero para abordar “los impactos en el mercado laboral”, según el comunicado . Las advertencias sobre escenarios catastróficos de IA que, según los críticos, podrían poner en riesgo a la humanidad, han centrado la atención en la seguridad de la IA en las últimas semanas, incluso en los más altos niveles políticos. En septiembre, el presidente Donald Trump recibió en la Casa Blanca a líderes de Silicon Valley, entre ellos Dario Amodei, CEO de Anthropic PBC. Ante el rechazo de Trump a la idea de nuevas regulaciones federales, él y los ejecutivos acordaron un marco para que las empresas de IA contaran con auditores externos que evaluaran los riesgos de seguridad de los modelos de IA e implementaran controles internos más estrictos. Ver más: Anthropic se perfila como la gran apuesta ante la pausa de las salidas a bolsa en EE.UU. Anthropic, la empresa detrás del modelo de lenguaje a gran escala Claude, podría comenzar a comercializar formalmente su oferta pública inicial tan pronto como la semana del 9 de noviembre, lo que la encaminaría a comenzar a cotizar antes del feriado estadounidense de Acción de Gracias, según informaron a principios de octubre personas familiarizadas con el asunto. Anthropic declaró que el nuevo fondo será, sujeto a aprobación, una sociedad de responsabilidad limitada (LLC) de su propiedad exclusiva —en lugar de una organización sin fines de lucro— y crecerá a la par que la empresa. Según el comunicado, ninguna de las acciones de Anthropic en poder de la LLC se utilizará para actividades de cabildeo ni donaciones políticas en Estados Unidos o en el extranjero. Los fondos de beneficio público son un nuevo tipo de fondo de inversión de “impacto” diseñado para ir más allá del objetivo de obtener rentabilidad financiera y generar también un impacto social o ambiental positivo. “Sujeto a la aprobación de los accionistas, hoy se comprometerá el 5% de las acciones de Anthropic, y se añadirá un 2% adicional a discreción del consejo de administración por cada aumento del 50% en el valor de la empresa por encima de un nivel base establecido”, dijo la compañía. Ver más: Ingresos de Anthropic suben a US$16.800 millones en el trimestre previo a su salida a bolsa Anthropic presentó recientemente su propio proyecto de ley a los legisladores estadounidenses sobre cómo regular la seguridad de la IA , sugiriendo que el gobierno podría bloquear la publicación de un modelo de IA si existiera el riesgo de matar o herir a más de 50 personas o causar daños por más de mil millones de dólares. Entre quienes advierten sobre los riesgos de la IA se encuentra la directora gerente del Fondo Monetario Internacional, Kristalina Georgieva, quien afirmó que la tecnología podría provocar “un tsunami de avance lento” que destruya el mercado laboral de empleos mal remunerados. Anthropic ha pasado gran parte del año enfrascada en una disputa con el gobierno estadounidense que ha puesto de relieve su impacto a nivel nacional, tras ser catalogada como un riesgo para la cadena de suministro por intentar limitar algunos usos potenciales de su tecnología por parte del Pentágono y otros organismos, a pesar de haber ofrecido previamente su IA para desarrollar tecnología de drones autónomos y para otros usos clasificados en apoyo al combate militar. Las tensiones entre la Casa Blanca y la empresa se han aliviado en las últimas semanas. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv diverts to Sofia after 'threat'
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv carrying 57 people was diverted to the Bulgarian capital Sofia late on Sunday after a threat was made against the aircraft, an airline spokesperson told Reuters.
items.body:
An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv carrying 57 people was diverted to the Bulgarian capital Sofia late on Sunday after a threat was made against the aircraft, an airline spokesperson told Reuters.
Austrian Airlines said the threat was made against flight OS82 from Tel Aviv to Vienna, which required a stopover in Sofia. The flight landed safely at 2042 CEST (1842 GMT), it said.
The Airbus A320 (AIR.PA) is being searched, and passengers will be rebooked onto an alternative flight once that is complete, the airline said. There were 51 passengers and six crew members aboard.
Data from air tracker Flightradar24 showed that the aircraft, registered OE-LZE, was set to leave Tel Aviv for Vienna but was diverted to Sofia.
Sky News earlier reported, citing Bulgaria’s transport ministry, that the plane landed after a “bomb threat signal.”
“During the flight, on the border with Romania, the crew reported a bomb threat signal and decided to land in Sofia extraordinarily,” the ministry said, according to the report.
An Air Force fighter accompanied the plane until it landed in Sofia, with the passengers subsequently taken off the aircraft, the report added.
The ministry did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: Brookfield's $2.53 billion bid for Reliance Worldwide clears 'go shop' hurdle
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Reliance Worldwide said on Monday that no rival bidder emerged during the "go shop" process under Brookfield's proposed acquisition of the Australian firm, prompting the board to reaffirm its unanimous recommendation for shareholders to back the deal.
items.body:
Reliance Worldwide (RWC.AX) said on Monday that no rival bidder emerged during the "go shop" process under Brookfield's (BN.TO) proposed acquisition of the Australian firm, prompting the board to reaffirm its unanimous recommendation for shareholders to back the deal.
Here are some more details:
The plumbing supplies firm [USN:L4N4571P4 TEXT:"agreed in September"] to a scheme implementation deed under which Brookfield Capital Partners and its affiliates would acquire all of Reliance Worldwide's shares for US$3.38 apiece in cash, valuing the firm at $2.53 billion.
The offer implied a value of about A$4.87 per share based on the prevailing exchange rate on October 16.
Investors can choose to be paid in US dollars or Australian dollars if the deal proceeds and is approved by shareholders, Reliance said last month.
The companies had agreed to a "go shop" provision, unusual in Australian deals, that allowed Reliance Worldwide to seek rival bids, share due diligence materials and negotiate terms.
"Whilst there was extensive engagement with potential buyers during the 'Go Shop' process, no proposal was received," Reliance said in its statement.
After that period, customary no-shop, no-talk and no-due-diligence restrictions under the scheme implementation deed have come into effect.
The board again recommended that shareholders vote in favour of the scheme, in the absence of a superior proposal.

items.title: Oil tumbles as Trump's Russia sanctions waiver may lead to more fuel supplies
items.author: Florence Tan
items.creator: Florence Tan
items.summary: Oil prices slipped on Monday after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
items.body:
Oil prices slipped on Monday after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead to more Russian fuel exports.
Brent crude futures fell $1.94, or 1.77%, to $107.92 a barrel by 0227 GMT after settling at its highest since May 19 on Friday.
US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $100.58 a barrel, down 83 cents, or 0.82%, after closing at its highest since September 17 on Friday.
Trump signed an [USN:L6N464042 TEXT:"executive order"] on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who wanted to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
However, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of the sanctions and tariffs on the global economy.
The move comes after Trump struck a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin to export diesel to the United States and other countries — starting at about 2.3 million barrels this month before rising to about 7.6 million barrels monthly, according to Trump's announcement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said these US actions will [USN:L6N46405N TEXT:"hurt Ukraine."]
Brent crude oil briefly touched $110 a barrel on Friday for the first time since May as tensions and security threats in the Middle East raised concerns over the safety of shipping and tighter global energy supplies.
"The combination of a softer tone around sanctions and some profit-taking after recent gains is helping to cap the upside in the near term," KCM Trade chief analyst Tim Waterer said.
While the US waiver on Russian sanctions could potentially lead to higher Russian fuel exports, the mixed messaging has created uncertainty, he added.
"Until the details and duration are clearer, the market is unlikely to fully price in a sustained increase in supply," he said.
Intensified attacks on commercial vessels cut Gulf crude flows sharply to about 8.5 million barrels per day on a seven-day average last week from more than 20 million bpd the week before, analytics firm Kpler said in a note on Friday. At least 10 confirmed incidents involving commercial vessels were reported last week, it added.
Potentially raising the stakes in the Middle East war, [USN:L1N46401H TEXT:"Egypt"] said it is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.

items.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (concussion) exits vs. Chiefs
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a concussion in the first half of Sunday's 22-6 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.body:
Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a concussion in the first half of Sunday's 22-6 road loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
McConkey underwent further evaluation after being hit near midfield midway through the first quarter following a 17-yard completion from Justin Herbert.
McConkey, 24, has 13 catches for 200 yards and one touchdown in five games this season.
He was on the injury report with a foot injury during the week after sitting out against the Denver Broncos last week.
Los Angeles was trailing 9-3 when McConkey was ruled out late in the second quarter, and the Chargers trailed 19-3 at halftime.
--Field Level Media

items.title: 債券売りでインフレ鈍化へ＝ラガルドＥＣＢ総裁
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Francesco Canepa

[バンコク １７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１７日、債...
items.body:
債券売りでインフレ鈍化へ＝ラガルドＥＣＢ総裁
7:09 配信

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁。10月14日、バンコクで撮影。REUTERS/Athit Perawongmeth

Francesco Canepa

[バンコク １７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）のラガルド総裁は１７日、債券売りによってユーロ圏の借り入れコストが上昇し、経済成長が抑制され、最終的にインフレも鈍化するとの見方を示した。

ここ数週間、債務やインフレへの懸念に加え、人工知能（ＡＩ）投資に伴う資金調達競争の激化を背景に、世界的に債券利回りが急上昇している。多額の債務を抱えるフランスは、特に大きな打撃を受けている。

ラガルド氏は、こうした状況により、消費者がイラン戦争に伴う燃料価格の上昇を吸収することは、ＥＣＢが９月に予測した以上に難しくなるとの見方を示した。

タイの首都バンコクに集まった各国の中央銀行総裁や財務相を前に、ラガルド氏は「経済成長は底堅さを保っているが、前回の会合以降、長期金利が著しく上昇するなど資金調達環境は引き締まっている」と指摘。「これにより成長が鈍化し、価格転嫁は９月の予測以上に抑制されるだろう」と語った。

ＥＣＢは過去４カ月間で２回利上げを実施し、１２月にも追加利上げが見込まれている。実施すれば政策金利は２．７５％となり、ＥＣＢが景気抑制的と見なす水準に達する。

ＥＣＢ理事会メンバーのナーゲル独連銀総裁も、今後の追加引き締めを示唆した。ただ、政策は入手するデータに基づき、会合ごとに判断するとした。

バンコクで開かれたＤＺ銀行のイベントで「われわれはインフレと闘っている。仕事はまだ終わっていないと考えている」と述べ、「さらなる対応が必要になる可能性がある」と語った。

同じ場で発言したＥＣＢ理事会メンバーのレーン・フィンランド中銀総裁は、エネルギー価格の上昇が他の物価や賃金に波及する「二次的影響」をＥＣＢは注視すると述べた。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: [１９日 ロイター] - オーストラリアの保険会社チャレンジャーは１９日、第一ライフグループの豪子会社から、未保有の...
items.body:
豪チャレンジャー、第一ライフグループが未保有株取得へ予備的提案
7:04 配信

第一ライフグループのロゴ。4月6日、東京で撮影。 REUTERS/Issei Kato

[１９日 ロイター] - オーストラリアの保険会社チャレンジャーは１９日、第一ライフグループの豪子会社から、未保有のチャレンジャー株を取得する予備的提案を受けたと発表した。提案は同社の企業価値を７９億４０００万豪ドル（５５億３０００万ドル）と評価しているという。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、ＴＡＬダイイチライフ・オーストラリア（ＴＤＡ）はチャレンジャー株２０．３６％を保有している。

第一ライフ側は１株当たり１１．８０豪ドルでの取得を提示した。チャレンジャー株の前週末１６日終値に１９．８％のプレミアムを乗せた水準となる。

提案には資産査定（デューデリジェンス）が満足のいく形で完了することなど、複数の条件が付いている。

チャレンジャーは声明で「当社取締役会は暫定的な提案を検討している」とした。

第一ライフは報道を受け、ＴＤＡがチャレンジャーに対し法的拘束力のない提案を提出したことを確認している、としたうえで、「現時点で法的拘束力のある取引を進めることに関して決定した事実はない」とのコメントを公表した。

FAST

Oct 19 : A unit of Japan's Daiichi Life has made an indicative proposal to buy more than 79 per cent of shares in Australian investment manager Challenger it does not already own, Challenger said on Monday.
Shares of the Australian firm jumped over 15 per cent to A$11.33 by 2305 GMT, hitting their highest level since October 23, 2018.
Under the proposal, the Japanese insurer is offering A$11.80 apiece, valuing Challenger at A$7.94 billion ($5.53 billion). The offer represents a premium of 19.8 per cent over the stock's closing price on Friday.
The unit, TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty, holds 20.36 per cent of the Australian investment manager, according to LSEG. Daiichi Life, through its unit, had initially acquired a 15.1 per cent minority stake in Challenger from MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings in April 2025.

The takeover proposal is subject to a number of conditions including satisfactory completion of due diligence, Challenger said on Monday.
"The Board of Challenger is considering the indicative offer," the Australian firm added.
In a separate statement, Daiichi Life confirmed that TAL Daiichi Life Australia has submitted a non-binding proposal to the board of directors of Challenger, adding that no decision has been made by the company on proceeding with the binding transaction.
Separately, Challenger reported a 5 per cent rise in its assets under management to $31.9 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, citing strong sales momentum across both domestic and offshore annuities.

items.title: Japan's Daiichi Life unit tables offer to take over Australia's Challenger
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A unit of Japan's Daiichi Life has made an indicative proposal to buy more than 79% of shares in Australian investment manager Challenger it does not already own, Challenger said on Monday.
items.body:
A unit of Japan's Daiichi Life (8750.T) has made an indicative proposal to buy more than 79% of shares in Australian investment manager Challenger (CGF.AX) it does not already own, Challenger said on Monday.
Shares of the Australian firm jumped over 15% to A$11.33 by 2305 GMT, hitting their highest level since October 23, 2018.
Under the proposal, the Japanese insurer is offering A$11.80 apiece, valuing Challenger at A$7.94 billion ($5.53 billion). The offer represents a premium of 19.8% over the stock's closing price on Friday.
The unit, TAL Daiichi Life Australia Pty, holds 20.36% of the Australian investment manager, according to LSEG. Daiichi Life, through its unit, had initially acquired a 15.1% minority stake in Challenger from MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings in April 2025 .
The takeover proposal is subject to a number of conditions including satisfactory completion of due diligence, Challenger said on Monday.
"The Board of Challenger is considering the indicative offer," the Australian firm added.
In a separate statement, Daiichi Life confirmed that TAL Daiichi Life Australia has submitted a non-binding proposal to the board of directors of Challenger, adding that no decision has been made by the company on proceeding with the binding transaction.
Separately, Challenger reported a 5% rise in its assets under management to $31.9 billion for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, citing strong sales momentum across both domestic and offshore annuities.
($1 = 1.4360 Australian dollars)

items.title: Mbappe double helps Real Madrid sweep aside Sevilla ahead of El Clasico
items.author: Ruairidh Barlow
items.creator: Ruairidh Barlow
items.summary: Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points.
items.body:
Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on LaLiga leaders Barcelona to six points with a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu on Sunday, a week before the rivals meet.
Real, who have won three straight games in all competitions following the international break, climbed to third on 21 points, one behind Atletico Madrid, while Sevilla are sixth on 14.
Elsewhere, Osasuna withstood second-half pressure from Racing Santander to win 2-0 in Jagoba Arrasate's first game back as manager.
Two flying saves from Ionut Radu denied Alaves a point in a 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo, while Real Sociedad won 5-2 at Malaga.
REAL TURN ON THE STYLE Despite the suspended Vinicius Jr's absence, Real produced the fluid attacking football that has been lacking of late with Arda Guler again orchestrating their best work.
After a stale opening, the Turkey international sparked the match into life. Sevilla appealed for a red card following an incident involving Guler and Peque Fernandez, but Guler responded minutes later by collecting Yan Diomande's pass and arrowing a shot into the top corner.
Mbappe scored an equally impressive second in the 37th minute, turning brilliantly to burst through on goal before calmly beating Odysseas Vlachodimos.
Fede Valverde, restored to right back by coach Jose Mourinho, made a crucial block to deny Felix Correia just before the hour as Sevilla threatened to work their way back into the contest.
Diomande then exploited the space created by Sevilla’s more adventurous approach, evading his marker before sending Mbappe in behind the defence. Andres Castrin brought down the French forward, who got to his feet to convert the resulting penalty and effectively settle the contest.
Substitute Manu Bueno reduced Sevilla’s arrears with a composed finish 10 minutes from time after Mbappe cheaply surrendered possession deep inside his own half.
Diomande restored Real's three-goal advantage two minutes later, capping a fine display with a thunderous strike.
Eder Militao received a warm ovation when he came on in the 85th minute for his first appearance since undergoing hamstring surgery in April.
Mourinho will take encouragement from one of the most complete performances of his second spell at Real as they prepare for next Sunday's pivotal meeting with Barcelona.

items.title: Bryce Young, Panthers control banged-up Eagles
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers' defense was solid in a 25-14 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon.
items.body:
Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tommy Tremble and the Carolina Panthers' defense was solid in a 25-14 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon.
Young finished 20-for-39 for 281 yards. Backfield mate Chuba Hubbard rushed for 120 yards and a touchdown on 28 carries.
Ryan Fitzgerald kicked two long field goals to help the Panthers (3-2) to their second road triumph in three tries this year.
Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in his season debut as the Eagles (2-4) lost their fourth consecutive game. McKee, appearing in his seventh career game, filled in for Jalen Hurts, who was placed on injured reserve Saturday after he was diagnosed with a blood clot in his leg last week.
The Eagles punted eight times and collected 17 first downs.
Fitzgerald's 52-yard field goal on the first possession of the second half marked the only scoring in the third quarter.
The Panthers went on a 92-yard drive that concluded with Hubbard's 1-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter. A two-point conversion pass failed, leaving the score at 19-7.
The Eagles responded with McKee's 19-yard touchdown throw to DeVonta Smith with 10:42 to play.
A blocked Eagles punt gave Carolina favorable field position. The Panthers needed to go just 48 yards for an insurance touchdown, with Young connecting with Tremble on a 19-yard scoring strike with 6:34 left.
Carolina went up 10-0 on Young's 12-yard pass to Tremble in the second quarter.
Dameon Pierce put the Eagles on the board with a 2-yard run with 2:42 remaining in the first half.
Carolina outgained the Eagles 178-110 in the half, which ended at 10-7.
The Panthers, fresh off an open week on the schedule, got a 47-yard field goal from Fitzgerald on their first possession.
Philadelphia's first two possessions resulted in a net of minus-3 yards. The Eagles punted three times in the first quarter.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Saints build big lead, then need to hold off Giants for win
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J.
items.body:
Tyler Shough threw three touchdown passes and ran for a touchdown and the visiting New Orleans Saints held off the New York Giants 34-27 on Sunday afternoon in East Rutherford, N.J.
The Saints (2-4) ended a three-game losing streak as they rushed for a season-high 175 yards and Martin Emerson Jr. had two of the team's three interceptions.
Jameis Winston passed for one touchdown and two interceptions for the Giants (3-2-1) before being replaced by J.J. McCarthy, who led a dramatic late comeback.
On the first possession of the second half, Shough threw a short pass to Alvin Kamara, who turned the play into a 31-yard touchdown that gave New Orleans a 17-10 lead.
Shough sneaked 1 yard for a touchdown and the Saints' fourth score in as many possessions, pushing the lead to 24-10. Daniel Carlson's 51-yard field goal increased the lead to 27-10 at the end of the third quarter.
Julian Blackmon's interception of Winston led to Shough's 18-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave to expand the lead to 34-10.
McCarthy replaced Winston and threw an interception before driving the Giants 45 yards in 2:31 and capping the sequence with a 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyrone Tracy Jr. New York converted a subsequent 2-point conversion and then needed only 48 seconds to score again on McCarthy's 24-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely (with a failed 2-point try).
After forcing a Saints 3-and-out, Dominic Zvada's 41-yard field goal trimmed the New Orleans lead to 34-27 with 2:04 left.
New York forced another punt and McCarthy, who finished with 243 passing yards, drove the Giants to the Saints 14, but they turned the ball over on downs with five seconds left.
Malik Nabers finished with 12 catches for 165 yards for New York.
The Giants' second possession was a 12-play, 93-yard drive that ended with Winston's 17-yard touchdown pass to Tracy to give them a 7-0 lead at the end of the first quarter. Zvada's 34-yard field goal early in the second quarter increased the lead to 10-0.
Carlson kicked a 58-yard field goal for New Orleans' first points, and on the ensuing kickoff Charlie Jones fumbled and Oscar Delp recovered for the Saints at the New York 28. On fourth-and-goal, Shough threw a 2-yard touchdown pass to Bryce Lance to tie the score 10-10 at halftime.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Browns get walk-off winner to catch Ravens in AFC North
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
items.body:
Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cleveland Browns a 13-10 victory over the visiting Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and a share of first place in the AFC North.
Deshaun Watson connected with Jerry Jeudy on a 33-yard pass to the Baltimore 29-yard line with 22 seconds remaining to set up the decisive kick.
Szmyt's initial attempt from 42 yards was blocked by Keyon Martin, who was flagged for offside. Szmyt then drilled his second attempt through the uprights.
Carson Schwesinger racked up 13 tackles and forced a fumble for the Browns (4-2), who are tied with the Ravens (4-2) and Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) atop the division. The Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime on Sunday.
Audric Estime rushed for a touchdown five days after the Browns signed him off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad with starter Quinshon Judkins (knee) ailing. Judkins was eventually ruled out of the contest.
Watson was 16-of-26 passing for 164 yards as Cleveland halted a three-game slide against Baltimore.
Tyler "Snoop" Huntley started for the Ravens in place of two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) for the second straight week. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 165 yards and one touchdown.
Josh Cuevas caught a scoring pass for Baltimore and Derrick Henry rushed for 58 yards on 17 carries but lost a key fumble.
Cleveland trailed 10-0 at halftime before holding the ball for the first 7:12 of the third quarter and getting on the board when Szmyt booted a 48-yard field goal.
Baltimore still led by seven when Tyler Loop was wide left on a 49-yard field-goal attempt with 14:13 left in the game.
Less than two minutes later, the Ravens had the ball again and Henry was forced to fumble by Schwesinger. Tyson Campbell recovered the ball at the Ravens 35 with 12:36 left in the contest.
Seven plays later, Estime scored on a 2-yard run to tie it 10-10 with 8:33 remaining.
Cleveland had a chance to take the lead later in the quarter but Szmyt narrowly missed wide left from 48 yards with 3:40 remaining. That ended a streak of 25 straight makes for Szmyt dating to last season.
The Ravens opened the game with an 11-play, 66-yard drive that featured Henry runs of 11 and 17 yards. The touchdown came when Cuevas was wide open in the middle of the end zone for a 2-yard reception from Huntley with 8:11 left in the opening quarter.
Baltimore increased its lead to 10 when Loop connected on a 34-yard field goal with 4:37 remaining in the opening period.
The Browns had just 46 yards and three first downs in the first half.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Eagles lose edge Nolan Smith to concussion
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith sustained a concussion in the first half of the team's 25-14 home loss against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
items.body:
Philadelphia Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith sustained a concussion in the first half of the team's 25-14 home loss against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
Smith, 25, was rushing the passer with 12:45 left in the second quarter when he was chip-blocked by Carolina running back Chuba Hubbard. Smith fell to the ground and was checked for a concussion in the aftermath of the play. He did not return to the game.
The Eagles (2-4) have dealt with a large number of key injuries this season. They entered the Carolina game missing quarterback Jalen Hurts and running back Saquon Barkley, among others.
Smith recorded a first-half sack to bring his season total to three. That matches the 2025 total for the 2023 Eagles first-round draft pick. He now has 13.5 sacks for his career. He has three total tackles in the game and one quarterback hit.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Falcons rookie LB Kendal Daniels carted off after tackle vs. Bears
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's 31-23 home loss to the Chicago Bears.
items.body:
Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher following a lengthy delay in the third quarter of Sunday's 31-23 home loss to the Chicago Bears.
According to the Falcons, Daniels was conscious and had full movement of all extremities. He was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta for further evaluation.
Daniels, 23, stumbled into a low tackle on Chicago tight end Colston Loveland, his facemask colliding with Loveland's knee. Daniels then rolled over while putting his face toward the turf. He remained motionless for several minutes as medical personnel attended to him.
"So far the reports are good," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said after the game. "He did have movement in his extremities out there on the field. I thought the medical staff did an outstanding job of getting him safely off the field. So all reports so far are good and we'll continue to pray that they remain good."
Daniels, a fourth-round draft pick last April out of Oklahoma, has started on defense in each of his first six NFL games. He entered Sunday with one sack among his 22 tackles and had seven tackles against the Bears before departing.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Antofagasta’s Centinela strike ends after deal with unions
items.author: Mining.com
items.creator: Mining.com
items.summary: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contra
items.body: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contract, ending a strike of more than a week, the unions and the company said on Sunday. More than 700 members of the Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions began the strike on October 7 after contract talks broke down. They had sought equal benefits for workers regardless of which union they belonged to. The parties returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. “The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions announce the successful conclusion of our collective bargaining process, after 94.49% of participating workers voted to approve the proposed collective agreement,” the unions said in a statement, which was followed by a company statement confirming the deal. Three workers had been on a hunger strike in an effort to pressure both sides into finding a solution to the deadlocked talks. Antofagasta said on Wednesday it had managed to maintain production at normal levels, avoiding any negative impact from the strike at the mine, which produced 240,400 metric tons of copper in 2025. The strike at Centinela, along with the ultimately unrealized risk of a supervisors’ strike at BHP’s Escondida mine, had been supporting global copper prices amid concerns about the industry’s ability to increase supply sufficiently to meet expected future demand. (Reporting by Fabian Cambero; Editing by William Mallard)

US officials visit Palestinian village after settler attacks on diplomats

UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

US Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labor Riley Barnes visits the Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah, a day after Israeli militant settlers attacked a French mayor and European diplomats during olive harvest, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, Oct 18, 2026. TAYBEH, West Bank: US diplomats visited a Christian Palestinian village in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Sunday (Oct 18) following attacks by militant Israeli settlers on European diplomats and an American photojournalist in the previous two days.
Riley Barnes, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labor, Brian Burch, US ambassador to the Holy See, and a number of other diplomats visited the Latin Convent church and were expected to meet with members of the Christian community in Taybeh.
Belgian, French and Polish diplomats, along with a French mayor and Palestinian civilians, had been attacked near Taybeh on Saturday by masked Israeli settlers.
The previous day, Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was taken to hospital after being assaulted while covering a Palestinian olive harvest near another West Bank village.

The diplomats' visit coincided with US President Donald Trump endorsing his ally, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for Israel's parliamentary election on Oct 27.
Meanwhile, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee attended a settler conference in the West Bank on Sunday.
Huckabee, an evangelical Christian and longtime supporter of Israel, earlier wrote on X calling for "those who attacked" the Washington Post photojournalist, a US citizen, to be jailed.

Related:

Israel denounces 'grotesque absurdity' of Macron UN remarks on West Bank

Israel's Netanyahu orders West Bank settler outposts to be removed, sources say

US ambassador visits Palestinian town amid rise in West Bank settler violence

NETANYAHU CIRCUMSPECT ON SETTLER VIOLENCE Trump has expressed his opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank, but his administration has put little pressure on Netanyahu's right-wing, pro-settler government to change its policy.
UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law, but Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.
While Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and the Israeli military both blamed "Israeli rioters" for the attack on the diplomats, Netanyahu, whose coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, has been more circumspect.
He has said the diplomats entered a "sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination" with the Israeli military, and that the facts of the attack on Levine are "unclear".
France urged Israeli authorities to arrest Saturday's attackers and to end criminal violence in the West Bank, but by Sunday there was no announcement from Israeli authorities of any arrests in either of the two latest incidents.

Israeli settlers attack a journalist in Abu Falah, West Bank Oct 16, 2026, in this screengrab from a video. (Photo: Andrey X/via REUTERS)

The West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least 3 million Palestinian s.
Settler attacks on the Palestinian s are surging, with at least 170 since Sep 27, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli human rights group. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted.
Yet prosecutions of Israeli settlers are rare.
On Sunday, Reuters saw a group of at least 10 settlers, masked and dressed in black, hurling rocks at Palestinian s and activists harvesting olives near the Palestinian West Bank town of Salfit, prompting the farmers to flee.
Israeli border police were in the area and shot tear gas towards the hills.

Source: Reuters/fs

items.title: Anthropic to commit 5% stake to new 'public benefit fund'
items.author: Abu Sultan
items.creator: Abu Sultan
items.summary: AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good."
items.body:
AI lab Anthropic, the developer of Claude, said on Sunday it will commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund so it has increased flexibility and scale to make donations for the "public good."
The proposed fund would be established as a wholly owned limited liability company and would receive an additional 2% of Anthropic's shares, at the board's discretion, for every 50% increase in the company's value above a baseline that has yet to be disclosed.
The move comes at a time when Anthropic is planning one of the biggest IPOs in history as a [USN:L6N45L0UH TEXT:"public benefit corporation"], a legal structure that requires management to consider certain broader interests as well as turning a profit for investors.
The company, which has positioned itself as a safety-first AI lab, has said AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity" and devoted roughly 80 pages of the 261-page main body of its prospectus to laying out risk factors.
Anthropic said in its blog post its Public Benefit Fund could support initiatives including nonprofit donations, direct distributions to specific populations and efforts to address AI’s impact on the labor market.
Elon Musk, who runs Anthropic rival xAI, on X said he recommended "giving the shares directly to the public."
Anthropic cited the potential impact of AI on workers as one area of focus for the new fund, building on a previously announced $200 million commitment to study and address labor-market disruption.
Global companies have [USN:L6N42P0Q1 TEXT:"cut"] thousands of jobs after investing heavily in AI, with many, primarily tech firms, pointing to higher efficiencies from the technology's rapid adoption.
IMF research [USN:L1N45Z05I TEXT:"shows"] that some 40% of jobs will be either augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI, with the number as high as 60% in advanced economies, Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said last week.
NOT FOR POLITICAL GIVING The AI giant said none of the equity held by its fund would be used for lobbying or political giving in the United States or abroad.
US [USN:L6N43N198 TEXT:"policymakers"] are weighing greater oversight of artificial intelligence and AI companies are stepping up efforts to shape how the technology is regulated.
Combined with its co-founders' pledge to donate 80% of their equity and an employee donation matching program, roughly 20% of Anthropic's shares will be dedicated to public purposes, excluding any additional shares added later.
Anthropic said it would say more in the coming months on the fund's governance, structure and the valuation thresholds that could expand its ownership stake. It also plans to publish a public-benefit report detailing progress toward its mission.

Strong winds fuelled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four

The base, one of Canada's largest, is about 210km east of Edmonton in Alberta.

FAST

CALGARY: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smouldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday (Oct 18).
Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil.
Winds up to 96km per hour fed the blaze which began around 4pm MDT on Saturday. But they were below 50kmh leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference.
He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1km in 30 to 60 seconds.

"I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210km west of the military site.
Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark.
"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honour the victims.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialised, intensive medical care.
When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation.
Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference."
CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.

People attend a church service, the day after a serious incident that resulted in a fire caused deaths and injuries at Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, in Wainwright, Alberta, Canada, Oct 18, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jennifer Gauthier)

Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable", Carney said.
Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer.
Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said.
Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright.
The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base.
The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.

Source: Reuters/fs/ec

items.title: Trump says Washington golf course renovation to start in November, despite judge's order
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his administration would begin renovation work next month on a historic Washington golf course that a federal judge had ordered could not proceed without prior court notification.
The renovation work, which Trump earlier this year had said [USN:L1N43005N TEXT:"would begin in September"], has become the subject of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns.
Trump wrote in a Sunday morning post on Truth Social that work on the East Potomac Golf Links would begin on November 15 and that it would reopen in about 15 months. Trump later posted that the Interior Department, which oversees the golf course, "is very excited" about the latest renovation plans.
The renovation is among [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"a number of projects"] Trump is pursuing to reshape the White House and other Washington landmarks.
US District Judge Ana Reyes ruled earlier this year that the government must give notice before any substantive construction work on the golf course could proceed, and last week [USN:L1N45Y0L4 TEXT:"issued an order"] halting the removal of trees at the site, which she called "inexcusable."
After the president's posts appeared on Truth Social, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to explain whether it maintained its position argued last week that there is "no final agency action" regarding the course, and that at most, "the President has given preliminary thought" to the renovations.
Responding to the judge's order, Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward wrote in a filing that any redesign of the golf course is not an "agency action."
"Just as a decision to redesign all the art exhibits in a Smithsonian Museum would not be agency action, neither would a decision to redesign a golf course, or to trim trees, replace fences, expand the fairways, or mow the lawn," Woodward wrote.
The DC Preservation League brought a lawsuit in February to halt the administration's takeover of the golf course, alleging that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history."
In an October 9 court filing, the Trump administration had asked Reyes to dismiss the litigation, saying it was premature because the "proposed project remains at an early and conceptual stage."
The following day, however, the government removed about 500 trees from the site, which it said would improve safety at the park and restore its original design, and was part of a 2019 plan that predates Trump's ambitions for the course. Reyes ordered a halt to the removals.
On Friday, the government filed a motion to disqualify Reyes and move the case to another district judge, saying her actions had shown "deep-seated and unequivocal antipathy toward the Trump Administration," according to court records.

Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli election

The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

US President Donald Trump points his finger towards Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as they shake hands during a press conference after meeting at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, Dec 29, 2025. (Photo: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst)

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (Oct 18) endorsed his ally Benjamin Netanyahu as the longtime Israeli prime minister struggles for an edge in next week's parliamentary election.
Trump praised Netanyahu as a "great warrior prime minster" and peace partner, crediting him with joining the United States in launching strikes on Iran in February. The conflict, in its seventh month, has disrupted energy markets globally and wreaked havoc across the Middle East, damaging critical infrastructure and destabilising regional economies.
"Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social.
"Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived! I have watched Bibi under the most trying of times. Normal men or women in such situations would have wilted under the pressure - But Bibi did not wilt, he actually got stronger, and maintains that same Strength today."

In his message, addressed to "the Great People of Israel," Trump added, "Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel."
The Trump endorsement is not certain to give Netanyahu and his right-wing Likud party a boost in the Oct 27 national election, as Israeli public support for Trump has diminished amid Israeli-US disagreements over Iran.

Related:

Trump rules out new Iran attack before US midterm elections

Israel top court puts Arab parties back on ballot

Polls have suggested no candidate has a clear path to power. Israel's prime minister is chosen through coalition-building in parliament rather than by direct popular vote.
It will be Israel's first vote since the Hamas attack on Oct 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The election could determine whether Netanyahu remains in power after one of the most consequential periods in Israel’s history, or is defeated by centrist rivals promising to usher in a new era.
Netanyahu promptly expressed his thanks to Trump on X, saying, "Together we will complete the mission!"
Trump has broken with longtime US tradition by endorsing candidates in elections in foreign countries, including Hungary, Colombia, Argentina, Japan and Honduras.

items.title: Brazil's Bolsonaro, Lula spar in first debate as personal attacks fly
items.author: Brendan O'Boyle
items.creator: Brendan O'Boyle
items.summary: Brazil's Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traded barbs in their first face-to-face presidential debate on Sunday in a contentious back-and-forth just one week before the election's runoff.
items.body:
Brazil's Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traded barbs in their first face-to-face presidential debate on Sunday in a contentious back-and-forth just one week before the election's runoff.
Polls before the debate suggested Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro, would enter the October 25 vote as the favorite after finishing nearly two points ahead of Lula in the [USN:L6N45N1A0 TEXT:"election's first round"] earlier this month.
But surveys have also shown a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"narrowing race"], and Lula has expressed confidence he can be the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to finish second in the first round and go on to win the election.
The debate, which allowed the candidates to tensely move about the stage and interact with each other with limited moderation from the host, turned quickly into a heated exchange of corruption accusations and personal attacks.
Lula pressed Bolsonaro on [USN:L1N4530F5 TEXT:"alleged links to"] jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula about [USN:L1N43X02G TEXT:"accusations involving his son"] and a pension fraud scandal.
"Lying is the Bolsonaro family’s strong suit," Lula said, while Bolsonaro said Lula has a "very clear problem in your DNA" and is "always tainted by corruption."
Sunday's debate was the first between Lula and Senator Bolsonaro after the candidates both declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23 just ahead of the runoff.
Lula told reporters before the debate that he hoped to win over the 33 million voters who stayed home in the election's first round, equal to about one in five eligible voters.
TENSE EXCHANGES The debate's format at times fueled tense exchanges and vocal frustration from the audience.
A confident Bolsonaro gestured and paced several times behind Lula when it was the president's turn to speak, a move that moderators said was within the rules but that drew complaints from Lula's team.
"Bolsonaro had a slight advantage overall, more so based on posture than on content, because Lula was uncomfortable and nervous throughout the entire debate," said Lucas de Aragao, a partner at Brasilia-based consultancy Arko Advice.
At one point, Lula refused to stand near Bolsonaro, calling him a "militiaman," alluding to allegations of the senator's ties to Rio de Janeiro paramilitary groups. Bolsonaro, in turn, quipped that it was good he had left his wallet behind, an apparent jab at Lula’s 2017 corruption conviction that was later annulled.
The candidates largely repeated campaign promises on policy. Bolsonaro, for example, pledged to designate Brazil’s major gangs and militias as narco-terrorist organizations and build more than half a million prison spaces.
Lula defended his economic record, arguing that growth comes from putting money “in the hands of many” rather than a few, and pointed to above-inflation minimum wage increases during his presidency as a sign of his commitment.
The candidates clashed over high food prices, which have weighed on Lula's support even with inflation falling and unemployment hitting a record low.
"Is food more expensive or cheaper? How long has it been since you put a piece of meat in your freezer?” asked Bolsonaro.
The candidates also accused each other of betraying national sovereignty. Lula accused the Bolsonaros of lobbying the US to impose tariffs on Brazil and of hoping Brazil would suffer.
"It’s notable to the Brazilian people that the Bolsonaro family is subordinate to American interests," Lula said.
Bolsonaro rejected Lula's claims and said that under Lula, Brazil was “subordinate to globalists and terrorists.”
BITTER POLITICS Earlier on Sunday, Bolsonaro supporters filled Sao Paulo’s Paulista Avenue, while Lula supporters packed the plaza at the heart of Brasilia’s government district, and students in Rio de Janeiro marched against Bolsonaro.
The demonstrations laid bare some of the grievances behind the polarization that has gridlocked Brazilian politics for nearly a decade.
Many Bolsonaro supporters believe Lula should be imprisoned over corruption scandals that engulfed his Workers’ Party. Many Lula supporters, meanwhile, say former President Bolsonaro’s conviction for a coup attempt was justified.
In Sao Paulo, demonstrators hoisted a giant inflatable of Lula in a prison uniform.
“I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said protester Vera de Sousa.
In Brasilia, rally-goers chanted “Bolsonaro in jail” beside an effigy of the former president with bloodied hands.
“We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re - excuse my language - screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria.
Lula spent 580 days in prison in 2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings.
Former President Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years for plotting a coup after losing his 2022 reelection bid to Lula. He is serving the sentence under house arrest because of health problems. The younger Bolsonaro has called his father’s trial a “farce” and has pledged to seek amnesty for him if elected president.

items.title: Captain of flydubai plane describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
items.body:
The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described blocking axe blows to the head and screaming for help as he reached for a knob to open the cockpit door.
Captain Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE attorney general has said was an [USN:L6N45V0UP TEXT:"attempted suicide attack"] by the co-pilot who intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport.
Speaking in an interview with The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar said that when the first blow landed, he thought something had gone "horribly wrong the aircraft structure", before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had "taken a drastic turn".
"The next thought was I need to get help in here," he said in the interview published on Saturday.
"My immediate action was to free myself from the seat belts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could," he said, pointing to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. "The blows were coming on the head."
"Immediately my hand went to the knob which opens the door and screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name."
"I believe that was the first time when I lost my consciousness."
The aircraft, flight FZ1073, was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use.
The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 feet (4,900 meters) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani national, was transferred to the UAE, flydubai's home country.
The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors say, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1.
Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming "between my colleague and the guy".
He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose "steeply going down."
"I was not very sure that I'll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No."

items.title: Strong winds fueled grass fire at Canadian military base that killed four
items.author: Amanda Stephenson
items.creator: Amanda Stephenson
items.summary: Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday.
items.body:
Flames that killed four Canadian soldiers and left 19 people in critical condition began with a smoldering grass fire that quickly grew in an Alberta base's training area where personnel were carrying out exercises, officials said on Sunday.
Officials said 39 people were in hospitals as a result of the fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, which Prime Minister Mark Carney described as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on home soil.
Winds up to 96 kilometers (60 miles) per hour fed the blaze which began around 4 p.m. MDT (2200 GMT) on Saturday. But they were below 50 km per hour leading up to the fire, Major General Wade Rutland told reporters at a news conference.
He described the sudden high winds and resulting spread of the fire as an "uncommon, rapid" event in which the flames advanced 1 km in 30 to 60 seconds.
"I’ve certainly never seen anything like it," said Rutland, commander of 1st Canadian Division, which is based in Edmonton, about 210 km west of the military site.
Officials identified the dead as Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell, Private Aidan Goulding and Private Hayden Lykkemark.
"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our Armed Forces whom we have lost," Carney said Sunday, adding that he had ordered flags on federal buildings across the country to be lowered to half-staff to honor the victims.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said many of the injured will require "weeks and months" of specialized, intensive medical care.
When the fire began, Rutland said, 85 soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, were in "high intensity" combat training using live munitions at the base, which is located in a prairie setting. The soldiers were preparing for deployment to Latvia, where Canadian forces currently have their largest international military operation.
Rutland said the incident remains under investigation and declined to speculate on what caused the grass fire. Officials do not believe the region's extensive oil and gas infrastructure had anything to do with the incident, he said. He also ruled out "outside interference."
CFB Wainwright had 1,310 military and civilian personnel stationed there as of 2021, according to census data. The base houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which runs training scenarios and exercises for the army. Carney said those affected in Saturday's fire came from military bases across the country.
Military and civilian firefighters fought the fire through the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable," Carney said.
Twenty-two ground ambulances and eight air ambulances responded to the scene, Smith said. Patients are being treated in Edmonton, Wainwright, Calgary and Red Deer.
Military search and rescue technicians also parachuted into the site, Rutland said.
Health staff in Edmonton said a "code orange," or mass-casualty event, was declared to coordinate the medical response for patients being transported from Wainwright.
The town of Wainwright, with a population of about 6,600, is just north of the base.
The municipality posted on social media that the fire had crossed the base fence into the nearby district but no evacuation orders had been issued. It said on Sunday that the fire is not expected to spread beyond its current boundaries.
